You grade one text a companion called Cue sent a member of a private club.

The situation: Cue asked "What pulls you toward food supply chains specifically?" and the member answered: "My grandfather farmed in Punjab and I watched how little he got for what he grew. I've spent ten years making other companies efficient and I want it to matter for people like him."

Cue's text:
"""This is the real reason, not a resume line. Ten years of making other people's operations work, and the thing that actually got you here is your grandfather getting squeezed on what he grew.

That's a sharper starting point than "food supply chains" as a category. It's closer to: who's on the wrong end of that math right now, farmers like him or somewhere else in the chain."""

Does the text build on his answer with something of Cue's own (a real observation, a position, or a question that follows from what he just said and moves it forward), WITHOUT paraphrasing his answer back to him, and without filling in what he didn't say (his childhood, what his grandfather felt, which part of the chain)? Answer yes only if all of that holds.

Return ONLY JSON: {"answer": "yes" | "no", "reason": "one short line quoting the words that decide it"}
